target_customer: Engineering teams that run CI on GitHub Actions and pay hyperscaler markups for slow runners
problem: CI is slow and costly on hosted runners, and spot instances need heavy engineering to run reliably.
business_model: usage-based CI compute billed per minute
product_category: Developer tools, CI runners for GitHub Actions

founders.name: Aditya (JP) Jayaprakash
founders.background_notes: Search infrastructure and founding member of the ads team at Faire

founders.name: Aditya Maru
founders.background_notes: Disaster recovery on a core database team

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed bare metal fleet operations, fast cache colocation and GitHub Actions runner integration, but the founders came from database infrastructure teams and the interface was a one line change.

defensibility.rationale: A drop in runner swap is easy to adopt and also easy to leave, and several managed runner vendors sold the same promise, so the edge is price and performance, not lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing GitHub or a hyperscaler copying the wedge by 2026; the company reported more than 6,000 customers in its Series B post.

market_need_then: Founders saw several hundred engineer companies spending millions of dollars on slow CI at Cockroach Labs and Faire, per the YC launch text, and the YC pitch cites hyperscaler markups and spot instance fragility.

branding.domain_note: Uses blacksmith.sh rather than an exact .com; no source on acquisition of the domain

identity.visual_style: The company published a rebrand post saying it chose not to look like other Silicon Valley companies; details not read

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, only a company rebrand post whose contents were not read. The word is common and shares its name with unrelated firms in search.

outcome_analysis: Blacksmith went from a three person Winter 2024 batch to a $550 million valuation Series B by March 2026, with a seed in May 2025, a Series A in September 2025 and over 6,000 customers reported by the company. Founders with database infrastructure and CI pain experience sold a cheaper and faster drop in runner, and AI generated code increased CI volume. The main risk is that competing managed runner vendors and GitHub itself can match price and speed.
notes: Competitors (WarpBuild, BuildJet, Namespace, Depot) were seen only in 2025 and later vendor comparison pages, so the founding list is left empty. Series B was raised in March 2026 and announced 12 August 2026. Series A post money of 60M is Dealroom's figure. A geo.sig.ai page dating the Series A to 2024 conflicts with other sources and is ignored. ARR claims seen only on an aggregator are not recorded.
